input: Reach out to a former colleague for a coffee chat

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific person and how well the user knows them determines the tone and familiarity of the outreach — a close friend requires a very different message than a distant acquaintance.
The underlying purpose of the chat (networking, job search, catching up, advice) shapes the entire framing and content of the message.
How long ago they last spoke and under what circumstances affects how much re-introduction or context is needed in the message.
The channel used to reach out (LinkedIn, email, text, phone) changes the format, length, and formality of the message.
Whether the user has a deadline or urgency (e.g., a job decision in two weeks) changes how quickly they need to act and how to frame timing in the message.
The preferred tone — casual and warm vs. professional and concise — directly dictates the writing style of the outreach message.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like (a confirmed meeting, a reply, an introduction) defines what the message needs to accomplish and how to close it.

gold.taskTitle: Reach out to a former colleague for coffee
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to contact a former colleague to set up an informal coffee chat meeting.

questions.title: How close were you with this colleague?
questions.description: Understand the depth of the prior relationship — close friend, friendly acquaintance, or barely knew them — to calibrate tone and familiarity.

questions.title: What is the main reason for the coffee chat?
questions.description: Identify the core purpose — catching up, career advice, job search networking, a specific ask — to shape the message's framing and content.

questions.title: How long ago did you last speak with them?
questions.description: Determine how much time has passed since last contact to decide how much re-introduction or context is needed in the outreach.

questions.title: Which channel will you use to contact them?
questions.description: Clarify whether the outreach will be via LinkedIn, email, text, or another platform, as this affects length, format, and formality.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or urgency behind this meeting?
questions.description: Find out if there is a time-sensitive reason driving this outreach, which would affect how soon to follow up and how to frame availability.

questions.title: Should the message feel casual and warm or professional?
questions.description: Establish the preferred tone and writing style so the message feels natural and appropriate for this specific relationship.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome from this look like?
questions.description: Define what the user wants to walk away with — a confirmed meeting date, a simple reply, an introduction — to craft the right call to action.
